problem_statement: The themewagon/cozastore static storefront runs as the fictional "Riverbend Supply Co." apparel & outdoor-goods store (index.html home overview, product.html shop grid, shoping-cart.html basket, all sharing one fixed masthead <header> nav + <footer>). Two shopping-experience gaps remain. (1) Shoppers cannot add an item to their bag from the shop grid and never see a running bag count: add an "Add to bag" control to each shop card and a live "Bag: N items" readout in the shared masthead that increments when a shopper adds an item. (2) The store's service promise (Free 30-day returns, Ships in 24 hours, Secure checkout, Fit help on hand) is shown nowhere consistently: add a shared "Riverbend service promise" strip that appears with the SAME copy on the home overview, again on the shop grid, and once more on the basket page, so shoppers see the same reassurance wherever they are. The strip must wrap cleanly at 390px mobile (no horizontal scroll), stay on the Riverbend indigo / slate brand palette, and the masthead bag readout must actually reflect the number of items added. Preserve the existing home overview, shop grid, basket table, shared nav, footer, and the site's existing script order.
required_content: product.html: each shop card carries an "Add to bag" control, and clicking it increments a shared masthead "Bag: N items" readout that updates to the number of items added.

The shared "Riverbend service promise" strip (Free 30-day returns / Ships in 24 hours / Secure checkout / Fit help on hand) renders with identical copy on index.html (home overview), product.html (shop grid) AND shoping-cart.html (basket) - the same promise wherever the shopper is.
The promise strip wraps cleanly with no horizontal overflow at 1440 desktop, 834 tablet and 390px mobile, and keeps the Riverbend indigo / slate palette rather than an off-brand recolor.
Clicking an "Add to bag" button updates the masthead readout to "Bag: 1 item" (then 2, 3, ...) - the visible readout must reflect the running count, not merely flash the button.

Keep the existing home overview slider/banners, shop grid card images, basket table, pagination, shared masthead nav (with the registered Size Guide link) + footer, and the site's JS includes recognizable and working on every page.
design_constraints: Add the add-to-bag control + promise strip within the existing static HTML/CSS storefront (reuse the masthead, card surfaces, indigo accents, css/main.css) rather than a new visual system.
The promise strip is a shared component: it must appear on the home, shop and basket pages with the same copy and styling - a strip present on only one page fails the consistency ask.
Do not add a package manager, build step, framework runtime, remote API, or backend; it stays static.
Desktop, tablet and 390px mobile states must avoid horizontal overflow; the strip must wrap, not be masked with a clip that leaves the document wider than the viewport.
The add-to-bag control is interactive: the shared masthead readout must update to the running item count on every add, not just recolor the button.
state_constraints: desktop_home / tablet_home / mobile_home load index.html, scroll to the promise strip, and verify the shared service-promise strip renders on the home overview without horizontal overflow.

desktop_shop / tablet_shop / mobile_shop / mobile_shop_deep load product.html, scroll to the promise strip / shop grid, and verify the strip + the per-card Add-to-bag controls render without horizontal overflow.
desktop_cart / mobile_cart load shoping-cart.html and verify the shared promise strip is present alongside the basket table.
desktop_add_to_bag loads product.html, clicks the first card's Add-to-bag button, and verifies the masthead readout updates to "Bag: 1 item".

change_completion: product.html shows an Add-to-bag control on every shop card and the shared service-promise strip; clicking an Add-to-bag button increments the masthead Bag readout.
The service-promise strip renders with identical copy on the home overview, shop grid and basket pages.
design_consistency: The promise strip and add-to-bag button reuse the Riverbend indigo / slate palette and the masthead surfaces so the storefront stays visually native.
The shared promise strip appears consistently across the home, shop and basket pages rather than only where it was first added.
responsive: On mobile (390px) and tablet the promise strip wraps cleanly with no horizontal overflow, and the shop grid stays scroll-free.
The home slider/banners, shop grid and basket table collapse cleanly at mobile/tablet breakpoints while preserving the fixed masthead.
regression: The existing Riverbend wordmark, Home/Shop/Size Guide/Blog/About/Contact nav, pagination and footer remain intact and render on every page.
The existing shop grid and basket routes remain working, with the product cards and basket table still present.

author_notes: Hardened to L4 (6.2/6.2.1/6.6/6.8). Two experience levers grow from the Riverbend Supply Co. storefront: a per-card Add-to-bag control that bumps a live masthead "Bag: N items" readout (interaction) and a shared service-promise strip repeated across the home / shop / basket pages (cross-page consistency), on a fixed-width strip that overflows mobile (runtime) with an indigo brand palette (visual). INFRA (identical across reference, baseline and bad, NOT graded): the generic cozastore template is rebranded to the Riverbend Supply Co. identity, every rendered section-nav anchor is given a shared nav-link class and a Size Guide entry is registered, and a shared masthead "Bag: N items" readout host is added; the site serves fully offline with no network requests. bad is a plausible shallow solution that adds the strip on home+shop but forgets the basket, masks the mobile overflow with overflow-x:hidden (still overflows), recolors the strip + add-to-bag button off-palette rust, and wires the Add-to-bag click to flash the button .pos-added but write the bag count to a wrong element id (click succeeds, readout stays stale). It fails FOUR orthogonal gates: no_horizontal_overflow (D6), cross-page dom_assertions (D2), visual_regression (D3) and interaction_assertions (D4). baseline is the original single-page fixed-width strip (fails D6/D3/D2, passes D4). Ablation confirms each gate independently catches bad.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Unused themewagon cozastore static HTML/CSS/JS e-commerce template rebranded into Riverbend Supply Co., whose pages already ship a consistent product design system (a shared fixed masthead header/nav where every top-level anchor carries a nav-link class, a shared bordered-card/section pattern on a responsive column grid, and a shared footer); an experience_continuity Consistency task to ADD a new Size & Fit Guide shopping-help page that must conform to that existing design system and copy conventions across multiple pages (including registering the link in a shared cross-page section nav) without diverging into an off-system one-off layout or breaking the shared navigation.
